Awesome Reverse Engineering 

 Featured: REA — Agent-oriented reverse-engineering tools, from application behavior to native binaries. By the creators of awesome-reverse-engineering.

 

A curated starting point for understanding binaries, applications, firmware, file formats, and protocols.

Find a tool by the work you need to do. Each entry describes its purpose; commercial tools are marked commercial . This is an initial selection, open to additions and corrections.

 Start here

 Your task Start with 
 --- --- 
 Learn assembly and reversing fundamentals Learning 
 Identify an executable and its capabilities File identification and triage 
 Read native code or step through it Native analysis and Debuggers 
 Trace calls or instrument a running program Dynamic instrumentation and tracing 
 Bypass anti-debugging, unpack or rebuild imports Deobfuscation and anti-analysis 
 Examine a suspicious file, process, or memory image Malware analysis 
 Inspect an APK, .NET assembly, or Java program Android and managed code 
 Inspect an iOS app, macOS binary, or Apple firmware iOS and macOS 
 Unpack a Python, Go, Flutter, or Hermes binary Language runtimes and packagers 
 Understand browser behavior or an undocumented protocol Web and protocols 
 Extract firmware or inspect a binary format Firmware and hardware and File formats 
 Reconstruct game memory structures, assets, or bytecode Game reverse engineering 
 Compare builds or audit binary diffs Binary diffing and patch analysis 
 Solve constraints, explore states, or lift semantics Symbolic execution and formal analysis and Instruction lifting and semantics 
 Accelerate an investigation with AI agents AI-assisted analysis

 Learning

 

- Azeria Labs - ARM assembly tutorials with exercises for learning registers, memory, and calling conventions.
- Compiler Explorer - Compiles code in the browser with many compilers and shows the generated assembly, for seeing how source constructs and optimization levels translate to machine code.
- Corkami - Visual references and posters explaining binary formats and file structures, including executable-format layouts.
- Corkami PoCs - Minimal and unusual executable and document samples for studying file-format edge cases and parser behavior.
- Hextree - Hands-on mobile and hardware reverse-engineering courses and interactive labs; Commercial , with some free content.
- Malware Analysis Training - Windows malware-analysis course with programming, Windows-internals, and reversing exercises; labs need a suitable Windows analysis environment.
- Malware Unicorn RE101 - Introductory Windows malware-reversing workshop covering x86 assembly, triage, and debugging; its VM-based lab instructions use older software images.
- Nightmare - Course built from annotated CTF challenges, progressing from assembly and reversing basics to binary exploitation.
- OpenSecurityTraining2 - Structured courses in assembly, architecture, debugging, and reverse engineering.
- pwn.college - Free courses with hands-on challenges in Linux, assembly, reverse engineering, and binary exploitation, run in a browser-accessible environment.
- Reverse Engineering by Kevin Thomas - Annotated assembly and reverse-engineering lessons across x86, x64, ARM, AVR, and RISC-V, with lesson-specific toolchain and hardware requirements.
- Reverse Engineering for Beginners - Free book connecting compiled C and C++ examples to assembly across several architectures.
- RPISEC Modern Binary Exploitation - Course materials and labs covering reverse engineering, memory corruption, and exploitation; no commits since December 2021, so labs may need older toolchains.

 Books

 

- Hacking the Xbox - Introduction to hardware reverse engineering through the original Xbox's security design; free PDF edition released by the author.
- Practical Binary Analysis - Covers ELF and PE internals, disassembly, binary instrumentation, taint analysis, and symbolic execution, with tools built in the exercises.
- Practical Malware Analysis - Hands-on introduction to static and dynamic Windows malware analysis with lab exercises; published in 2012, so some tooling chapters are dated.
- The Ghidra Book - Guide to Ghidra's disassembler, decompiler, scripting, and extension APIs; the 2026 second edition covers BSim and PyGhidra.

 File identification and triage

 

- capa - Identifies capabilities in executable files using rules over static or dynamic analysis results.
- checksec - Checks ELF security properties such as PIE, RELRO, stack canaries, and non-executable stacks; mitigation flags are not a vulnerability verdict.
- Detect It Easy - Identifies executable formats, compilers, packers, and other file characteristics.
- FLOSS - Recovers obfuscated strings, including strings constructed on the stack.
- hexvero - Statically triages Electron archives and JavaScript bundles for IPC channels, preload bridges, and window settings, plus ELF/Mach-O/PE imports and hardening; its CLI, MCP server, and local web UI require Node.js 22.12+, and pattern-based JavaScript analysis can miss indirect code.
- LIEF - Parses and modifies executable formats such as PE, ELF, and Mach-O from code.
- Malcat - Hex editor and disassembler for triaging unknown files, with 50+ format parsers, embedded-file extraction, YARA scanning, and Python scripting. Commercial , with a free Lite edition for non-professional use.
